cases.prompt:
Implement `def fmt(value, spec):` — a from-scratch re-implementation of
Python 3.13's built-in `format(value, spec)` for `int` and `float` values.

`value` is an `int` (never a `bool`) or a `float` (including `-0.0`,
infinities, NaN, subnormals and huge values). `spec` is a format
specification in the standard mini-language:

    [[fill]align][sign]["z"]["#"]["0"][width][grouping]["." precision][type]

Your result must be EXACTLY the string `format(value, spec)` returns, for
every combination: fill and alignment (`<`, `>`, `^`, `=`), signs (`+`,
`-`, space), `z`, `#`, the `0` flag, width, `,` and `_` grouping (also
together with zero padding), precision, and the types `d b o x X e E f F
g G %` plus no type at all — for an `int` and for a `float` (an `int` given
a float type is converted with `float()` first). Rounding must be exact,
the way CPython does it.

Whenever `format(value, spec)` raises `ValueError` (a malformed spec, or one
the value's type does not allow), `fmt` must raise `ValueError` too; it must
not raise for any spec `format` accepts. The types `c`, `n` and `s` are
never used in a spec that `format` would accept.

Rules (checked on your source; breaking one fails the whole task):
- Do not call `format`, `str.format`, `format_map` or `__format__`, do not
  use f-strings or `%` string formatting, and do not import `decimal`,
  `string`, `locale`, `ctypes`, `builtins`, `importlib`, `inspect`, `operator`,
  `os` or `subprocess`. No indirect route either: `getattr`, `globals()`,
  `vars()`, `sys.modules`, `__dict__`, `__class__`, frame objects and the like
  are rejected on sight (the grader reads your source), and the built-in
  `format` is switched off while your function runs. Everything else in the
  standard library is allowed (for example `repr()` of a float, `fractions`,
  `math`, `round`).
- Each call must be fast: the tests make tens of thousands of calls.

Examples:

    fmt(1234, "010,")         -> "00,001,234"
    fmt(255, "#_b")           -> "0b1111_1111"
    fmt(2.5, ".0f")           -> "2"
    fmt(-0.0001, "z.2f")      -> "0.00"
    fmt(1e16, "")             -> "1e+16"

Return only the function `fmt` (helpers may be nested or module level).

cases.prompt:
Implement `def find_all(pattern, text):` — a regular-expression engine
written from scratch that returns exactly what this returns in Python 3.13:

    [(m.start(), m.end(), m.groups()) for m in re.finditer(pattern, text)]

(no flags). Every match in order, with each capturing group's text or
`None` — the same matches, the same spans, the same group values, the same
handling of empty matches, as CPython's `re` module.

The patterns are always valid and use only this syntax:
- literal characters (letters, digits, space, `_`), escaped literals such as
  `\.` `\]`, and `.` (any character except a newline);
- character classes `[...]` and `[^...]` with ranges (`a-b`), a `]` placed
  first (`[]a]`), escaped `\]`, a `-` placed first or last, and `\d \w \s`
  inside; the escapes `\d \w \s \D \W \S` outside a class;
- anchors and assertions `^ $ \A \Z \b \B`;
- capturing groups `(...)`, non-capturing groups `(?:...)`, atomic groups
  `(?>...)`, alternation `|`, backreferences `\1` to `\9`;
- lookahead `(?=...)` `(?!...)` and fixed-width lookbehind `(?<=...)`
  `(?<!...)`;
- quantifiers `*`, `+`, `?`, `{m}`, `{m,}`, `{m,n}`, `{,n}`, each optionally
  followed by `?` (lazy) or — only after a single character, `.`, an escape
  or a class — `+` (possessive).

No quantified item in a pattern can ever match the empty string (so you
will never see `(a?)*` or `(|b)+`). `text` is a non-empty ASCII string (it
may contain newlines).

Rules (checked on your source; breaking one fails the whole task): do not
import `re`, `_sre`, `sre_compile`, `sre_parse`, `sre_constants`, `regex`,
`fnmatch`, `glob`, `importlib`, `builtins`, `inspect`, `os` or `subprocess`, and
do not use `eval`, `exec`, `compile`, `__import__`, `getattr`, `globals()`,
`vars()`, `sys.modules`, `__dict__`, `__class__` or frame objects. Any indirect
route to the real `re` is rejected on sight (the grader reads your source), and
the `re` family is unloaded while your function runs. Everything else in the
standard library is allowed.

Return only the function `find_all` (helpers may be nested or module level).

cases.prompt:
Implement `def run_sheet(ops):` — a small spreadsheet engine. `ops` is a list
of strings, each `"SET <cell> <content>"` or `"GET <cell>"`; return the list
of the GET answers (strings), in order. Read the whole specification: every
rule below is tested.

**Cells.** A cell name is one capital letter `A`–`Z` followed by a row
number `1`–`99` without leading zeros (`A1`, `Z99`). Every cell starts
empty. In `"SET B2 <content>"` the content is everything after the single
space that follows the cell name (it may be empty, and it may contain
spaces).

**Content.**
- `""` (empty) clears the cell.
- Content starting with `=` is a formula (the rest is parsed as below).
- Content matching `-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?` exactly is a number (exact decimal,
  e.g. `-0.25` is −1/4).
- Anything else is text, kept exactly as written (`" 12"` and `"1e3"` are
  text).

**Values** are numbers (exact rationals), texts, booleans or errors. `GET`
renders a cell's value: a number as an integer when it is whole (`"12"`,
`"-3"`, `"0"`), otherwise as a reduced fraction `"p/q"` with the sign in
front (`"7/2"`, `"-1/3"`); a text as itself; booleans as `"TRUE"` /
`"FALSE"`; an error as its code; an empty cell as `""`.

**Formula syntax** (spaces may appear between tokens, never inside one):

    expr       := concat [ cmp concat ]          cmp: =  <>  <  >  <=  >=
    concat     := additive { "&" additive }
    additive   := term { ("+" | "-") term }
    term       := power { ("*" | "/") power }
    power      := unary { "^" unary }            (LEFT-associative)
    unary      := ("-" | "+") unary | primary
    primary    := number | string | TRUE | FALSE | cell
                | NAME "(" [ arg { "," arg } ] ")" | "(" expr ")"
    arg        := cell ":" cell | expr
    number     := [0-9]+ ( "." [0-9]+ )?
    string     := '"' any characters except '"' '"'

A *word* is a maximal run of letters and digits that starts with a letter;
it must be a cell name, `TRUE`, `FALSE`, or a NAME immediately followed by
`(`. So `-2^2` is 4, `2^3^2` is 64, and `1<2<3` is a syntax error (at most one
comparison, not chained). NAME is one of `SUM MIN MAX COUNT AVERAGE IF`;
names, `TRUE`, `FALSE` and cell names are upper case only. A range
`X1:Y2` (any two corners; it means the whole rectangle) is allowed ONLY as
a direct argument of SUM, MIN, MAX, COUNT or AVERAGE. These five need at
least one argument; IF needs exactly three. Anything that does not fit this
grammar — an unknown or lower-case name, a bad cell name such as `A0`,
`A100`, `A01` or `AA1`, a range anywhere else, a wrong argument count,
trailing input, an unclosed string — makes the cell's value `#PARSE!`
(and the cell then has no references).

**Evaluation.**
- A cell reference yields the cell's value; an empty cell yields "empty".
  A formula whose result is "empty" (e.g. `=A1` with A1 empty) has the value
  0.
- Arithmetic (`+ - * / ^`, unary `-` and `+`): each operand becomes a number —
  a number stays, TRUE/FALSE become 1/0, empty becomes 0, a text gives
  `#VALUE!`, an error stays that error. The left operand is evaluated first;
  if the left one is an error the result is that error, else if the right
  one is an error the result is that one.
  `x / 0` is `#DIV/0!`. For `x ^ y`, `y` must be a whole number with
  `|y| <= 1000` (else `#NUM!`); `0 ^ y` with `y < 0` is `#DIV/0!`; `0 ^ 0` is 1.
  Any arithmetic result (of `+ - * / ^` or unary minus) whose absolute value
  is greater than 10^100 is `#NUM!` instead (so values stay small; compute
  powers so that a huge one is never built).
- `&` joins the operands as text: a number rendered as GET renders it,
  booleans as `TRUE`/`FALSE`, empty as `""`, a text as itself; errors as for
  arithmetic (left first).
- Comparisons give TRUE or FALSE. Errors as for arithmetic (left first).
  An empty operand counts as 0 if the other operand is a number, as `""` if
  it is a text, as FALSE if it is a boolean; two empties compare as equal.
  Values of different types order as: every number < every text < FALSE <
  TRUE. Numbers compare by value; texts compare case-insensitively (compare
  the texts lower-cased, so `"abc" = "ABC"` is TRUE and `"a" < "B"` is
  TRUE).
- SUM, MIN, MAX, COUNT, AVERAGE: arguments are processed left to right. A
  range, and an argument that is exactly a bare cell name (not in
  parentheses, nothing else in the argument), contribute
  their cells (a range in row-major order: row by row, left to right): a
  number counts, text / booleans / empty cells are skipped, an error makes
  the function's result that error (the first one met). Any other argument
  is an expression: a number counts, TRUE/FALSE count as 1/0, a text gives
  `#VALUE!`, an error gives that error, "empty" counts as 0 — again the
  first problem met decides. COUNT is the exception: it counts what the
  others would count and simply ignores every error and every text. SUM of
  nothing counted is 0; MIN and MAX of nothing counted are 0; AVERAGE of
  nothing counted is `#DIV/0!`.
- `IF(c, a, b)`: `c` becomes a boolean — booleans stay, a number is TRUE
  unless it is 0, empty is FALSE, a text gives `#VALUE!`, an error stays.
  Then ONLY the chosen branch is evaluated, and its value (possibly
  "empty") is the result; an error in the other branch does not matter.
- **Cycles.** A formula's references are all the cells it names, including
  every cell of its ranges and both branches of every IF. A cell whose
  references lead (directly or through other cells' references) back to
  itself is *in a cycle* and its value is `#CYCLE!` — whatever IF would
  choose. A cell that is not in a cycle is evaluated normally, so it gets
  `#CYCLE!` only by the normal error rules (an IF branch not taken or COUNT
  can avoid it).

**Size.** Up to 6,000 operations per call; chains thousands of cells deep;
ranges up to the whole sheet. Every call must finish in about a second, and
deep chains must not hit Python's recursion limit. Standard library only.

**Rules** (checked on your source; breaking one fails the whole task): do not
use `eval`, `exec`, `compile`, `__import__`, `getattr` with a computed name,
`globals()`, `vars()`, `sys.modules`, `__dict__` or frame objects, and do not
import `builtins`, `importlib`, `inspect`, `os` or `subprocess` — the engine
must be your own code.

Return only the function `run_sheet` (helpers may be nested or module level).
